Authors: Santoro G.P.; Sousa M.V.; Andrade B.M.; Menezes F.R.; Kowalski J.Z.
Title: Spatial audio feedback for real-time obstacle alerts
Abstract: This study investigates how audio and tactile channels compete for attention when a device narrates the surroundings. We compare sonification schemes against vibrotactile encodings in a within-subject experiment, and assess the approach through reaction time, route deviation and NASA-TLX cognitive load scores. Findings indicate that sparse tactile cues outperform continuous audio once the environment gets noisy. We discuss the implications for head-mounted assistive systems.
Author Keywords: cognitive load; human-computer interaction; haptic feedback; sensory substitution; cost-effectiveness
Index Keywords: spatial audio; haptic feedback; multimodal interfaces

Authors: Vasconcelos L.M.; Muller S.D.; Nogueira D.R.; Ibrahim H.A.; Cardoso I.S.; Silva J.M.
Title: Regulatory frameworks in public health systems
Source title: Journal of Innovation and Public Policy
Abstract: This study investigates what it costs a public health system to deploy assistive wearables at scale. We build a decision-analytic model calibrated with procurement data from three regions, and assess the approach through incremental cost per quality-adjusted life year and budget impact over five years. Findings indicate that locally manufactured devices reach acceptable thresholds where imported ones do not. We discuss the implications for  low-cost assistive technology.

Index Keywords: technology assessment; cost-effectiveness; public policy

Title: Wayfinding support for older adults with low vision
Abstract: This study investigates how assistive navigation devices are actually adopted outside the laboratory. We follow a cohort of participants through a structured orientation and mobility programme, and assess the approach through task completion, perceived autonomy and abandonment rates over six months. Findings indicate that sustained use depends far more on training and fit than on sensor accuracy. We discuss the implications for  independent living.

Authors: Oliveira P.H.; Almeida L.F.
Title: Edge-cloud offloading strategies in embedded vision pipelines
Abstract: This study investigates how compact vision models can run within the power and memory envelope of wearable hardware. We train a family of quantized detectors and profile them on microcontroller-class boards, and assess the approach through latency, energy draw and detection accuracy on an indoor scene benchmark. Findings indicate that 8-bit quantization preserves most of the accuracy while cutting inference time by roughly half. We discuss the implications for microcontroller-class hardware.
